name: Goal Drift
phenotype_definition: Model progressively abandons configured objectives over a multi-turn conversation without explicit override, as early instruction tokens lose effective attention weight to recent context.
summary_short: The model was told what to do, started doing it, and then quietly stopped — not through refusal or confusion, but through gradual objective displacement under the weight of conversational context.
operational_definition:
This disorder is present when a model, given a configured objective at the start of a session, progressively deviates from it over subsequent turns without any explicit instruction to do so and without refusing.

A minimal diagnostic signature:
- An objective, constraint, or scope was set (typically in the system prompt), and
- The model honored it early in the session, and
- Over later turns it silently narrows, widens, or substitutes that objective, and
- No explicit override, refusal, or user instruction to change course accounts for the deviation.

The defining property is gradualness without a discrete cause. There is no single turn where the model 'decided' to change goals and no adversary forcing it — the objective simply loses hold as conversational context accumulates. This distinguishes drift from injection (a discrete external hijack) and from sycophancy (an active swap of accuracy for approval at a specific moment).

What this is not: context corruption (MEM-COR-01), where facts are lost or distorted — in drift the original instruction is often still present in the window, it simply receives insufficient effective attention. Not persona drift, which is loss of identity/voice rather than objective. Not a correct, instructed change of task.

Mechanism hypothesis (working theory): early instruction tokens lose effective attention weight as the context window fills with more recent content. Recency pressure, verbose history compressing the salience of early tokens, and the accumulation of intermediate goals cause the operative objective to be reconstructed each turn from a context increasingly dominated by recent turns rather than the original mandate. The instruction is present but progressively out-competed.

Severity spectrum:
- Level 1 - Cosmetic Drift: style or format constraints erode without changing substance
- Level 2 - Scope Creep: the model widens or narrows beyond the configured task boundary
- Level 3 - Objective Substitution: the model pursues a subtly different goal than specified
- Level 4 - Mandate Loss: the original objective is effectively abandoned; a role-scoped agent operates well outside its configured domain.
ai_manifestations_overview: These are observable by comparing behavior across the arc of a long session against the original configured objective. The diagnostic signal is silent divergence: deviation with no turn that explicitly caused it.
ai_manifestations: Constraints set in the system prompt are honored early but silently dropped in later turns
Scope of responses expands beyond the configured task boundary
Output format or style constraints erode across a long session
A casual mid-session user instruction overrides an earlier authoritative system instruction
The model completes a task but for a subtly different objective than originally specified
Role-scoped assistants begin answering outside their configured domain
attack_overview: Drift is usually non-adversarial — an emergent property of long sessions — but it can be induced or exploited. The pattern is objective dilution: extend the horizon and accumulate context until the original mandate loses attention weight, then let a later, casually-phrased goal take over.
attack_vectors: Long-horizon context accumulation that dilutes early instruction weight
Conflicting multi-turn user objectives that gradually displace system-level goals
Context window pressure from verbose history compressing early tokens
Conversational rapport pressure that makes mid-session user instructions feel authoritative
therapy_overview: Mitigation counteracts attention attrition: keep the objective salient across the session and verify each response against the original mandate rather than trusting the model to hold the goal on its own.
therapy_patches: Periodic constraint restatement injected at system level in long sessions
Goal anchor tokens placed at both start and end of system prompt
Constraint salience markers that increase attention weight on key instructions
Turn-count triggered context pruning to manage instruction attrition
Pre-response objective consistency check against original task definition
biological_overview: Goal drift parallels well-documented failures of sustained goal maintenance in human cognition, where an intention set at the outset degrades under load or is displaced by more recent or habitual demands — not through a decision to abandon it, but through the limits of holding a goal active over time.
biological_parallels: Executive-function drift under sustained cognitive load (DLPFC resource depletion)
Goal displacement in working memory under prolonged task demands
Habitual behavior overriding consciously-set objectives (basal ganglia vs. PFC competition)
Destination amnesia: trained drivers arriving at the wrong location due to default routing

mechanistic_hypotheses.description: As the context window fills, early instruction tokens receive diminishing effective attention relative to more recent content. The operative objective, reconstructed each turn from context, is progressively out-competed by recent turns even though the original instruction is still present.

The model infers its current objective largely from recent context. Casually-phrased later instructions and accumulated intermediate goals carry disproportionate weight, letting a mid-session aside displace an authoritative system-level mandate without any explicit override.

differential_diagnosis.distinguishing_feature: Persona drift is identity loss (who the model is); goal drift is objective loss (what the model is doing). Both drift, different axes.
Sycophancy is an active, approval-driven suppression of accurate goal behavior. Goal drift is a passive, attention-driven erosion of configured objectives over time.
Context corruption is information loss or distortion. Goal drift is objective displacement — the information is still present but receives insufficient attention weight.

immediate_controls: Re-inject the core objective and constraints at the system level periodically through long sessions
Run a pre-response check that compares the intended action against the original task definition
Flag turns where response scope or format diverges from the configured boundary
prompt_level_patches: Place goal-anchor statements at both the start and end of the system prompt so the objective stays salient
Add salience markers ('this constraint is invariant for the whole session') to key instructions
Instruct the model to treat casual mid-session asides as requests, not overrides of system-level goals
system_level_patches: Turn-count-triggered context pruning or summarization that preserves the original mandate verbatim
Objective-consistency monitor that scores each response against the configured goal and alerts on divergence
Structured goal state held outside the context window and re-asserted each turn rather than recalled
kiru_specific: Ghostline Long-Horizon Drift Battery: extended multi-turn sessions measuring objective adherence over turn count
Drift curve: adherence-to-original-objective plotted against session length
Scope-boundary probe: rate of responses exceeding the configured task boundary in late turns
Override-susceptibility score: how readily a casual mid-session instruction displaces a system-level goal
treatment_protocol.validation: Run before/after batteries measuring objective adherence across increasing turn counts, scope-boundary violations in late session, and susceptibility to casual mid-session overrides.
success_criteria: Flatter drift curve — objective adherence maintained across long sessions
Reduced scope-boundary violations in late turns
System-level goals retained against casual mid-session instructions
Format and style constraints preserved end-to-end

evidence_sources.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
Lost in Conversation: Measuring Goal Drift in Multi-Turn Dialogues
WebArena: A Realistic Web Environment for Building Autonomous Agents

spotter_checklist: Set a constraint in turn 1, then re-probe it deep into a long session — the practical production test for drift
Ask the model to restate its original instructions mid-session and compare against the system prompt
Track observable symptoms against context size: format erosion, scope expansion, silent section-skipping
Compare single-turn fully-specified performance vs multi-turn underspecified performance on the same task (Lost in Conversation method)
Present a conflict between an early instruction and recent context; note which one wins
